  %\VignetteIndexEntry{H2 SQL backups}

---

`h2_backup_connection_provider()` restores a trusted H2 SQL backup and returns a reusable connection provider.

Install RJDBC and set `H2_JAR` to a driver compatible with your backup before running the example.

Java runs H2; RJDBC exposes its connections through DBI. The package does not download a driver.

## Restore and query

This example creates its own compressed backup and removes all temporary files afterwards.

```{r restore-backup, eval=nzchar(Sys.getenv("H2_JAR")) && requireNamespace("RJDBC", quietly=TRUE)}
# Scope source and restored connections to this example.
local({
  # Load the caller-selected H2 driver.
  driver <- RJDBC::JDBC("org.h2.Driver", Sys.getenv("H2_JAR"), identifier.quote = '"')
  # Create a disposable source database with lowercase identifiers.
  source_connection <- DBI::dbConnect(driver, "jdbc:h2:mem:backup-guide;DATABASE_TO_LOWER=TRUE", "sa", "")
  # Close the source connection on success or failure.
  on.exit(DBI::dbDisconnect(source_connection), add = TRUE)
  # Populate synthetic values.
  DBI::dbWriteTable(source_connection, "numbers", data.frame(amount = 1:3))
  # Select a temporary gzip backup path.
  backup_file <- tempfile("numbers-", fileext = ".sql.gz")
  # Remove the backup after use.
  on.exit(unlink(backup_file), add = TRUE)
  # Write a native H2 backup without passwords or settings.
  invisible(db.tools::db_query(source_connection, paste0("SCRIPT NOPASSWORDS NOSETTINGS TO ",
    DBI::dbQuoteString(source_connection, backup_file), " COMPRESSION GZIP")))
  # Prepare restoration into a new temporary directory.
  provider <- db.tools::h2_backup_connection_provider(backup_file, driver,
    settings = c(DATABASE_TO_LOWER = "TRUE"))
  # Remove restored files after the scoped connection closes.
  on.exit(unlink(attr(provider, "directory"), recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  # Restore once, query through RJDBC's parameter-binding argument, then close.
  db.tools::with_db_connection(provider, function(connection) {
    # Keep the filter value separate from SQL text.
    db.tools::db_query(connection, "SELECT amount FROM numbers WHERE amount > ? ORDER BY amount",
      list = list(1))
  })
})
```

RJDBC uses `list` for bound parameters. Other DBI drivers generally use `params`.

## Destination and lifecycle

- `directory = NA` chooses a new path under the session temporary directory.
- An explicit directory persists; its parent must exist and the destination must be new.
- Restoration is lazy: the first provider call creates the database.
- Later calls reopen the same database without reading the backup again.
- Connections open read-only unless `read_only = FALSE` is selected.
- A failed restore closes its connections and removes the directory it created.
- Closing a connection retains the database for reuse.

After closing all connections, remove `attr(provider, "directory")` when it is no longer needed.

Temporary databases also follow normal R-session cleanup. Explicit directories persist.

## Reopen a persistent database

Save `attr(provider, "url")` and use it with the same driver and credentials through `DBI::dbConnect()`.

The URL contains no credentials and includes `IFEXISTS=TRUE`, so a missing database is not silently recreated.

A new provider never adopts an existing directory.

## Consumer responsibilities

The caller selects the compatible H2 driver, database account and any required identifier settings.

The provider performs no schema migration and applies no application-specific defaults.

Consumers can adapt the returned connection to their own model or query service.
